criteria: MVP first: classify every concern as blocking, hardening, or completeness, and report blocking concerns first. A concern is blocking only if, left unfixed, the software does not demonstrably do what it claims. Do not manufacture completeness concerns to avoid an empty return -- "no concerns, and here is what I checked" is a valid answer.

Does every goal predicate of the plan (RP1-RP5) have evidence in the results that would fail if the predicate were false? Read the phase records 002-phase-RP2.md through 006-phase-RP5.md and the tests they cite before judging.

Do the shipped code paths (src/gnd/export/pyrel_rules.py, src/gnd/export/ossie_formulas.py, src/gnd/export/emit.py, src/gnd/commands/export.py) behave as the results and delta say: same verdict as gnd check on every input the programs accept, a named exit-3 refusal for every input they cannot represent, the default (checker) export and the Ossie export unchanged?
Does docs/runtimes/pyrel.md state correctly, per target (DuckDB, LQP), what the rules programs check, list as not checked, and refuse?
Is every open question of the plan and the phase records dispositioned in plan section 11, and is each close amendment A1-A7 supported by the record that raised it, with the prior wording kept?
Every concern's evidence must cite one of the three named files; name the record, code or test line in the observation.
